log: Meshes 0 and 1 have identical triangle counts and component sizes but centres at x=+0.08 and x=-0.08: two copies of the same object side by side, one per material (SpecGloss vs MetalRough-style 'MR'). I named them Right/Left by world x; 'right' means +x, which is a guess about handedness/viewing direction.
Mesh 0 gives no colour at all ('no texture'), so its names rest on position and size only; mesh 1 colours (dark, red, tan) were used for mesh 1 names.

Nothing in the evidence tells what the object is for. Component 2 (tall, 0.246) spans the full height and overlaps component 0 (low, wider, 0.099) in y, so component 0 may be a base, a shell around the lower body, or something else; I used shape-descriptive names for it (Wide_Lower_Section). Component 1 (small, at the top, 0.039 tall) is named only as top piece, not as cap/stopper/lid. 'Body' for the tall component rests on size and position only.

Material names (BottleMat_SpecGloss, BottleMat_MR, Label Material MetalRough, Label Material SpecGloss) were used as evidence for the bottle/label reading and to separate the two copies, but are not listed in basis as instructed.

Label meshes: two flat quads (size z = 0, 0.150 x 0.019) at z=0.0 and z=1.0 of their own mesh, so a front and a back; mesh 3 repeats mesh 2's geometry with the other half of the UV atlas (v 0.5-1 vs 0-0.5) and no colour. I cannot say how they relate to the bottles (their at is relative to their own tiny mesh, so I do not know whether they sit on one bottle, between the two, or on both) and I did not attach them to a bottle. Front/Back follows +z/-z, again a guess about orientation. The label is wider (0.150) than a bottle (0.100) which is odd; left unresolved.

Mesh 3 labels got names by role ('Overlay') only because the second material duplicates the first's geometry; I do not know what that second layer is (e.g. a different texture channel); the name describes position in the plan only.
